title: ALP System Manifest v1
description: The single derived projection of a board.yaml that `west alp-emit system-manifest` (python -m alp_orchestrate --emit system-manifest) emits to build/system-manifest.yaml. It is the IDE / tool CONTRACT for a (possibly multi-image) project: one entry per per-core slice with its runtime, build directory, output artefact, and flash recipe, plus the IPC links and helper MCUs. Tools read THIS instead of re-deriving folder layout / build wiring from board.yaml + the SoM presets. Generated by the `alp_orchestrate` package (`python -m alp_orchestrate`); this schema and that emitter move in lockstep (a check gate validates the emitter output against this contract). Stability: schema_version 1 is additive-only (new optional fields only); a breaking change ships as schema_version 2 through a deprecation cycle, so consumers should tolerate unknown fields.  That advice and this file's `additionalProperties: false` are not in conflict, though they read that way: the closed root is a PRODUCER gate -- it is what makes `scripts/check_system_manifest.py` catch an emitter key typo instead of shipping it -- while tolerating unknown fields is CONSUMER advice, for a tool reading a manifest emitted by a newer SDK than it was built against.  Do not relax the root to make a consumer's life easier; a consumer that hard-rejects unknown keys is the thing to fix.

eeprom.description: Resolved features.hw_info.eeprom manifest location, when declared in board.yaml.

slices.description: One entry per per-core image. core_id + os + the build/flash wiring the IDE needs to build, run, debug, and flash each image without re-deriving anything.

os.description: Resolved runtime (zephyr | yocto | baremetal | off); the value-set is owned by metadata/schemas/board.schema.json cores.<core>.os.

app.description: Relative path to this image's app source dir (binds the core to its sub-folder).

recipe.description: Yocto bitbake recipe packaging this slice's `app:` source dir (required for an app-only Yocto slice; `app:` is a path, not a recipe name).

build_dir.description: Per-slice build directory (build/<core_id>-<os>); populated by fan-out.

output_artefact.description: Built image path; populated after a successful build.

flash_method.description: Backend the flasher dispatches to (e.g. zephyr_west_flash, yocto_wic_to_sd_or_emmc).

flash_args.description: Method-specific flash arguments (shape varies by flash_method).

ipc.description: Inter-core links (rpmsg / mailbox) with their resolved carve-outs. A blocked link carries status:blocked + reason instead of the carve-out fields.

helper_mcus.description: On-module helper MCUs (e.g. the GD32 bridge) that ship their own firmware image. Each key the SoM preset's `helper_firmware:` entry declares is projected here independently -- a helper may carry a field-update channel AND a local flash method at once (the GD32 bridge does), so a consumer must not read one key's presence as excluding another's.

flash_args.description: Method-specific flash arguments, or the string 'TBD' when a helper MCU's flash recipe isn't yet finalized in the SoM preset.

flash_policy.description: WHO may invoke `flash_method`, and WHEN, projected verbatim from the SoM preset. REQUIRED -- there is no absent-means-`customer` default. `customer`: a plain flash target. `factory`: Alp Lab programs it in production; never a customer flash target. `recovery_only`: Alp Lab programs it in production and the customer may flash it ONLY to recover a bricked device, with Alp Lab-supplied binaries. Independent of `update_channel`.

update_channel.description: How this helper's firmware is updated in the FIELD (`alp_ota_spi_otp` for the CC3501E's own OTP, `alp_ota_spi_bridge` for the GD32 bridge's slot-A/B application bootloader). Deliberately unenumerated here: the SoM-preset schema owns the vocabulary, and this manifest is additive-only for consumers that must tolerate a channel added upstream. Its presence does NOT mean the helper has no flash method.

boot_order.description: Resolved inter-image boot sequencing (empty until a SoM declares boot_order).

storage.description: Resolved storage partitions (present only when the project declares storage).

memory.description: Resolved memory-region view of the SoM: the regions `resolve_memory_map()` yields, each with the flash/RAM class derived from the SoC's declared aperture and the region's authored `write_authority` (#1365).  DECLARED AHEAD OF ITS PRODUCER, DELIBERATELY -- no emitter writes this key yet.  The emit half is deferred on FIXTURE CHURN, not on an open decision: emitting this key rewrites every `system-manifest.yaml` under tan's planner-oracle corpus (98 files, 94 of them carrying `ipc: []`), and landing that as its own single-cause diff is what keeps it reviewable. Ownership is already settled -- ADR-0026 section D decided alp-sdk's emitters are canonical and that `tan` consumes plan-embedded bytes rather than re-implementing the renderers -- and this schema is alp-sdk's under every migration outcome anyway (ADR-0026 clause 2). Declaring the contract here moves no emitted byte.  A consumer must therefore read an ABSENT `memory:` as "this producer does not emit it yet", NEVER as "this SoM has no memory regions".  Rows join the other panes by NAME: `ipc[].region` and `storage[].flash_device` each name a `memory[].name`.  That join is partial by construction -- an `on_module.ospi_memories:` key is a legal `storage[].flash_device` target but is a controller-instance name carrying a `capacity_mbit` and no base, so it lies outside every aperture and gets no `memory[]` row.  Partitions stay in `storage[]` and carve-outs in `ipc[]`; this array is the SoM-declared regions those two refer INTO, not a third copy of them.

items.description: One resolved region.  `name` is the join key.  A region whose base does not resolve carries no `base` and says why (`status: unresolved` plus a `reason`) instead of guessing one -- an absent derived field means unresolved, never a default (ADR-0034 clause 4).  `dt_label` appears only when verified against the board `.dts` (#1556), never as the name-derived fallback.
